newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FinMin says Sweden cannot postpone EMU decision.
newsitem.headline: FinMin says Sweden cannot postpone EMU decision.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Tuesday the country could not put off making a decision on whether or not it would participate in the currency union of the European Monetary Union (EMU).

"You can think what you like about EMU. But if EMU becomes a reality -- and there is much to suggest that it will -- then, we have to prepare ourselves for a Europe with an economic and monetary union. We won't be able to avoid taking a stance then," Asbrink said in an article in Swedish tabloid Aftonbladet.
In the article, which was written jointly by the finance minister and Social Democratic party secretary Ingela Thalen, the two said the decision, regardless of what it was, would affect the economy.
"Whether we join the EMU, elect not to take part or postpone the decision, our stance will affect the Swedish economy. Each alternative has its price, its advantages and disadvantages," they said.
Calling for an open debate on the issue, Asbrink and Thalen said the demand for price stability and balance in public sector finances would be just as great whether or not Sweden participated in EMU.
